semantic_slots.objects: The full real orthogonal group G = Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) R, its underlying real matrices O and Q, determinants and transposes, identity I_n, finite coordinate vectors x, A(O) = ((kappa + 1)/2) I_n - ((kappa - 1)/4)(O + O^T), the literal real function p(O,x) = sqrt(det A(O))/(2*pi)^((n:R)/2) * exp(-(x dot (A(O)x))/2), and full normalized Haar probability mu = Measure.haarMeasure (top : PositiveCompacts G).
semantic_slots.domains: n : natural numbers; kappa : real numbers; O,Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) R with both determinant signs; x : Fin n -> R; underlying matrices : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R; p : G -> (Fin n -> R) -> R. G has inherited real matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. mu is probability Haar on the whole compact G. Scalar formulas and integral values are real. The exponent ((n:R)/2) uses real division, not truncated natural division.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: For every implicitly bound n : N, every proof of 3 <= n, every implicitly bound kappa : R, and every proof of 4 <= kappa, let p be the stated formula. Then: (for every x : Fin n -> R, Integrable (O |-> det(O) * p(O,x)) mu) AND (for every Q : G and every x : Fin n -> R, the two displayed integrals are equal). O is separately bound inside the integrability function and each integral.
semantic_slots.assumptions: The only external hypotheses are 3 <= n and 4 <= kappa. O and Q are orthogonal by their carriers. Compactness and probability normalization of full Haar are supplied internally. There is no arbitrary measure, special-orthogonal restriction, assumed integrability premise, density-identification premise, or newly constructed probability law associated to p.
semantic_slots.conclusion: For each vector x, O |-> det(O) * p(O,x) is actually absolutely Bochner L1 under full Haar mu. Simultaneously for every orthogonal Q and every vector x, integral_G det(O) * p(O,Qx) dmu(O) = integral_G det(O) * p(O,x) dmu(O). The action Qx is matrix mulVec, and integration includes both determinant components of O(n).
semantic_slots.scopes: The binders n, its lower-bound proof, kappa, and its lower-bound proof scope over the let-defined p and the entire conjunction. The first universal x scopes only over the integrability conjunct. The later universal Q and x scope over the integral equality. O is separately bound in each integral. The same p and mu are used throughout. The external determinant multiplier is det(O), while sqrt applies to det A(O). The exponential argument is -(x dot (A(O)x))/2. In p(O,Qx), Qx replaces both vector occurrences in this quadratic expression. The power exponent is ((n:R)/2).
semantic_slots.constant_dependencies: No existential or unspecified constants occur. The numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and pi are fixed. G, its identity matrix, and normalized Haar mu depend on n. A depends on n, kappa, and O; p depends on n, kappa, O, and x. Integrability holds for every x, and invariance for every Q and x, with no additional parameter restrictions.

reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n satisfying n >= 3 and every real number kappa satisfying kappa >= 4, let G = O(n) = Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) R be the full real orthogonal group, including both determinant signs, and let mu = Measure.haarMeasure (top : PositiveCompacts G) be normalized Haar probability on the whole group, with the inherited real matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra. Let V = (Fin n -> R); vectors are finite real coordinate functions. For O in G, identify O with its underlying real n by n matrix and set A(O) = ((kappa + 1)/2) I_n - ((kappa - 1)/4)(O + O^T). Define the literal real function p : G -> V -> R by p(O,x) = sqrt(det A(O)) / (2*pi)^((n:R)/2) * exp(-(x dot (A(O)x))/2). Here sqrt is the nonnegative real square root, the displayed power is a real power with real division after coercion of n to R, dot is the finite Euclidean dot product, and matrix action is matrix-vector multiplication. Then the conjunction of these assertions holds: (1) for every x in V, the function O |-> det(O) * p(O,x) is Bochner integrable in the actual absolute L1 sense under mu; (2) for every Q in G and every x in V, integral over G of det(O) * p(O,Qx) dmu(O) equals integral over G of det(O) * p(O,x) dmu(O). In the second assertion Qx is the action of the underlying matrix Q by matrix-vector multiplication. The function p is specified pointwise as a real-valued formula; it is not a newly constructed probability law and no premise identifying a density is imposed.
